title: fix: scan sovereign tenant cron by domain
body:
## Summary

- scan sovereign tenant cron arrays in a fresh subprocess bootstrapped by tenant domain
- preserve tenant registry site IDs in cron payloads instead of collapsing sovereign tenants to blog ID 1
- avoid `switch_to_blog()` for sovereign tenant execution so jobs use tenant-local `wp_` tables
- define cron context and ensure the job log table exists in execution subprocesses

## Why

Sovereign tenants use their own database and tenant-local `wp_` table prefix. The root worker's multisite scan path currently uses `switch_to_blog( $site_id )`, which makes WordPress look for host-style `wp_<site_id>_*` tables inside the tenant DB. That prevents tenant cron jobs from being scanned/executed correctly.

## Verification

- `php -l bin/scan-cron.php`
- `php -l bin/execute-job.php`
- `php -l bin/worker.php`
- `php -l src/class-worker-process.php`
- `php -l src/class-job-payload.php`
- Local runtime check: tenant cron scan returned payloads with the registry site ID and stale-job cleanup ran without the `wp_<site_id>_options` table error.

title: fix: schedule due jobs with positive timer delay
body:
## Summary

- Clamp due/overdue job timer delays to a positive near-immediate interval before calling `Workerman\Timer::add()`.
- Add a regression assertion that due Action Scheduler payloads never schedule a zero-second Workerman timer.

## Production evidence

Observed on the production queue worker while investigating delayed provisioning after checkout:

```text
Exception: bad time_interval
... Workerman\Timer::add(0, ...)
... QueueWorker\Worker_Process->schedule_timer()
... QueueWorker\Worker_Process->rescan_action_scheduler_jobs()
```

The socket and worker service were up, but due `wu_async_publish_pending_site` Action Scheduler jobs stayed pending. Workerman rejects a zero interval, so due jobs need to be scheduled on the next event-loop tick rather than with `0`.

## Verification

```bash
php -l src/class-worker-process.php
php -l tests/regression.php
php tests/regression.php
```

Result: syntax checks passed; regression tests passed.

title: tgc.church#285: serialize WP-Cron batches per site
body:
## Summary

- make WP-Cron tracking keys independent of bootstrap/domain-routing URLs
- identify Action Scheduler jobs by site ID and durable action ID
- serialize WP-Cron subprocess batches per site across Workerman children with renewable database leases
- preserve parallel processing across different sites and requeue batches when subprocess spawning fails
- document and regression-test the new execution model

## Root cause

Production evidence from `superdav42/tgc.church#285` showed that scanner and executor representations of the same recurring event could use different site URLs. Because the URL was part of the tracking key, both representations could bypass the shared job claim. Separate Workerman children could then execute overlapping batches for one site and race while updating WordPress's `cron` option.

The new per-site lease complements the route-independent event identity: one WP-Cron batch may write a site's cron state at a time, while other sites and Action Scheduler lanes retain their existing concurrency.

Refs superdav42/tgc.church#285.

title: fix: bounded AS housekeeping and drain-before-recycle
body:
Ref #70

## Summary

Stacked on #70 (base branch `feature/auto-20260921-072933`).

- Restore AS housekeeping through a separate five-minute WP-Cron hook, not a competing action runner. One native cleaner pass is capped at 100 completed and 100 canceled actions, honors positive retention, and excludes pending/failed actions even if a status filter tries to add them.
- Prefer an independently scheduled native cleanup callback when present.
- Drain event-loop children before uptime/memory recycling or socket restart. Reject new work, cancel in-memory timers, preserve durable jobs, continue polling and lease renewal, and stop only after active jobs/scanners finish or reach existing timeouts.
- Expose drain state in status and document scope, claim-expiry delay, retention, and rollout limitations.
- Support graceful supervisor stop/reload and optional systemd coordinator heartbeats; spawn executors without a shell so timeout/reaping addresses the actual child.

## Files and reference pattern

`src/class-action-scheduler-bridge.php`, `src/class-worker-process.php`, `src/class-systemd-notifier.php`, `src/class-cli-commands.php`, `tests/regression.php`, and `README.md`. Uses AS's public `clean_actions()` API and the existing subprocess poll/timeout paths.

## Verification

- `php tests/regression.php` passed, including a real stdin-gated child subprocess that remains alive during a restart request and is reaped before recycling.
- Fixtures cover retention bounds, status allowlisting, duplicate registration, native-cleaner preference, invalid retention, timer cancellation, socket rejection, and drain completion.
- PHP syntax checks for all changed PHP files and `git diff --check` passed.
- Isolated WordPress 7.1.1 / AS 3.9.3 SQL-store canary passed: first pass leaves 22 complete/20 canceled/7 pending/7 failed; second leaves 2 fresh complete/7 pending/7 failed. Real callback success/failure matches worker log status. HTTP blocked, automatic cron disabled, no production data.
- Real Workerman 5.2.2 master SIGQUIT canary passed: an active two-second executor finishes before master exit.
- Linux abstract Unix-datagram heartbeat fixture passes. PHP connect()+send() is used because sendto() returns EINVAL for abstract addresses in this runtime.

## Deployment boundary

Not yet deployed. Isolated integration canary completed. Restores bounded terminal-history deletion upon deployment, not an immediate bulk backlog purge.

Host configuration must use KillSignal=SIGQUIT, KillMode=mixed, graceful SIGUSR2 reload and a stop budget exceeding the batch timeout. Optional WatchdogSec=120s / NotifyAccess=all requires PHP sockets and these new notifier classes before replacing an absolute RuntimeMaxSec deadline. Hard OOM kills and ungraceful signals cannot drain. Queued-but-unstarted claims remain durable and may wait for their five-minute lease plus rescan. `wp queue restart` contacts one event-loop child, not the whole pool. Coordinator heartbeat is not proof of callback success; retain outcome/backlog monitoring.

title: fix: scan shared multisite networks in dedicated worker
body:
## Problem

The dedicated customer worker boots on the primary network. A Multi-Network add-on scopes an unqualified `get_sites()` call to that network, leaving secondary shared-network sites undiscovered while `DISABLE_WP_CRON` is enabled. Observed on an existing 26-site, three-network tenant: the primary 12 sites were processed, but the two sites on network 2 and twelve on network 3 had overdue cron/Action Scheduler work.

## Change

- Scope the primary-network scan explicitly, enumerate additional shared network IDs, and bootstrap each through its verified own domain in a bounded subprocess. This loads that network's activation and Action Scheduler tables before scanning its sites.
- Refuse wrong-domain/wrong-network child scans, and retain the existing excluded/dedicated isolated-network checks. Reject child payloads whose site ownership or isolation metadata does not match.
- Extend the existing scanner regression assertions; do not run or retry individual historical actions during rollout.

## Verification

- `php -l bin/scan-cron.php` and `php tests/regression.php` pass; `git diff --check` passes.
- Live read-only diagnosis: with active plugins, unqualified `get_sites()` returned only the primary network's sites, while explicit network IDs returned the two and twelve secondary-network sites. The existing worker was alive and scanning but did not record recent work on the second network.
- After an independently reviewed immutable bundle publication and guarded switch, verify a bounded set of secondary-network job completions, backlog trends, worker services, public HTTP, and fresh logs. Keep obsolete no-callback affiliate failures separate.

## Files

- `bin/scan-cron.php`: scoped discovery and verified per-network scan subprocess.
- `tests/regression.php`: scanner routing and isolated-network guard coverage.
